newsitem.title: USA: Honey Baked Hams to pay penalty in ad case--USDA.
newsitem.headline: Honey Baked Hams to pay penalty in ad case--USDA.

text.p: Honey Baked Hams Inc, a food retailer, has agreed to pay a $125,000 penalty to settle a civil lawsuit brought by the U.S. Agriculture Department, the government announced Tuesday.

Under terms of the settlement, the firm, based in Irvine, California, would clarify the wording of its ads and give consumers more accurate information about the perishability of its spiral sliced glazed hams, the USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service said.

FSIS said the firm would not represent the hams as cured with spices and herbs, smoked over hickory or applewood chips, glazed with honey, or containing "lower sodium" or "less salt" unless it could substantiate the claims. It also would change the wording on its labels about storage and perishability of the hams to conform with California health and safety codes.

The lawsuit arose out of a complaint filed by the Santa Clara County Department of Environmental Health which alleged the firm violated state laws on misleading advertising and unfair competition. The complaint was the result of an investigation by FSIS and California officials.
